name: Darius the Mede
title: The Median King over Babylon
summary: Darius the Mede was the king who took control of Babylon after the fall of the Babylonian Empire. He is known from the book of Daniel, where he appointed Daniel to a high position and later was tricked into throwing Daniel into the lions' den. He recognized Daniel's God as the living God.

keyEvents.title: Takes Control of Babylon
keyEvents.description: Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of 62, after the fall of the Babylonian Empire.

keyEvents.title: Appoints Daniel to a High Position
keyEvents.description: Darius set 120 satraps over the kingdom and three administrators over them, with Daniel as the chief because of his excellent spirit.

keyEvents.title: Tricked into Issuing the Decree
keyEvents.description: The administrators and satraps tricked the king into issuing a decree forbidding anyone to pray to any god or man other than the king for 30 days.

keyEvents.title: Throws Daniel into the Lions' Den
keyEvents.description: Reluctantly, Darius had to throw Daniel into the lions' den, but he expressed hope that Daniel's God would rescue him.

keyEvents.title: Daniel Found Alive
keyEvents.description: Early in the morning the king hurried to the lions' den and found Daniel unharmed because his God had sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

keyEvents.title: Proclaiming Daniel's God
keyEvents.description: Darius issued a decree that all in the kingdom should fear Daniel's God, the living God who had rescued Daniel from the lions.
